answer.text: Where the current closing price is relative to the high-low range over a set period, indicating momentum

explanation.text: The Logic: The Stochastic Oscillator is a momentum indicator that locates the current closing price within the high-low trading range of a lookback period (typically 14 sessions). When the close sits near the top of the range it implies strong momentum and a potentially overbought condition; when it sits near the bottom, the opposite. Readings above 80 are conventionally treated as overbought and readings below 20 as oversold. The Trap: Long-term economic trends, total market capitalisation, and a company's earnings growth rate are not what the Stochastic Oscillator measures — those are macro or fundamental concepts, whereas Stochastic is a price-based technical momentum tool. Note: The cited NISM Series XV Research Analyst workbook (pp.303-304, 320, 326) refers to the Stochastic Oscillator only as a momentum indicator/tool for detecting overbought or oversold conditions; the explicit high-low-range closing-price formula used above is not stated on the pages checked. The formula description reflects general industry definition of the Stochastic Oscillator.
